title: Week 8 Mastery Quiz · Courts, Rule of Law, and Accountability

questions.question: Fictional judgment: a court strikes down an executive order but gives no remedy to people harmed by it. What remains unresolved?
options: Invalidation alone compensates every person affected by the executive order.
Availability and enforcement of effective relief
The judgment automatically ensures implementation without administrative compliance.
Only constitutional interpretation matters; remedial procedure is irrelevant to legal accountability.
questions.explanation: Availability and enforcement of effective relief

questions.question: A study reports faster cases after court reform but omits appeal and reversal rates. Which limitation matters?
options: Timeliness alone does not measure accuracy, rights protection, or procedural fairness
questions.explanation: Timeliness alone does not measure accuracy, rights protection, or procedural fairness

questions.question: Simulated disciplinary rules let the executive remove judges without independent review. What institutional risk warrants investigation?
options: Pressure on judicial independence through insecure tenure
questions.explanation: Pressure on judicial independence through insecure tenure

questions.question: Two courts reach different outcomes under similar statutes. What is the soundest method for comparison?
options: Compare facts, jurisdiction, legal text, interpretive methods, and procedural posture
Count the number of words in the judgments
questions.explanation: Compare facts, jurisdiction, legal text, interpretive methods, and procedural posture

questions.question: A public prosecutor reports 95% conviction rates. Which claim is warranted without more evidence?
options: The figure alone cannot establish trial fairness or prosecutorial independence
Conviction rates prove the rule of law
questions.explanation: The figure alone cannot establish trial fairness or prosecutorial independence

questions.question: An investigative report alleges bribery but relies on an unnamed single source. Which evidentiary next step is strongest?
options: Seek corroborating financial records, procedures, and independently verifiable testimony
questions.explanation: Seek corroborating financial records, procedures, and independently verifiable testimony

questions.question: Fictional statute guarantees legal representation, yet remote residents wait a year for counsel. Which distinction matters?
options: The statute is meaningless in every case
Formal entitlement versus practical and equitable access to legal assistance
questions.explanation: Formal entitlement versus practical and equitable access to legal assistance

questions.question: A court ruling interprets a constitutional right narrowly, while a later authenticated amendment broadens the text. What research action is required?
options: Trace dates and authoritative texts before claiming the earlier ruling controls the new language
questions.explanation: Trace dates and authoritative texts before claiming the earlier ruling controls the new language

questions.question: A post-conflict commission hears survivor testimony but lacks authority to prosecute. Which description is most precise?
options: It is identical to a criminal tribunal
Truth-seeking and criminal adjudication have different mandates and standards
Its evidence can never be useful
questions.explanation: Truth-seeking and criminal adjudication have different mandates and standards

questions.question: Court budget records show rising allocations, while legal aid participation falls. What should the senior scholar conclude?
options: Legal aid is unrelated to courts
Budget totals and service access diverge; investigate allocation, costs, demand, and outcomes
questions.explanation: Budget totals and service access diverge; investigate allocation, costs, demand, and outcomes

shortResponse: When can courts constrain political power, and what makes judicial independence credible?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
